newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates stable,awaiting new cash reserve.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates stable,awaiting new cash reserve.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were stable on Tuesday and dealers foresaw little movement ahead of the expiry of the current cash reserve arrangement on Thursday.
"Call money could slip a little more on Wednesday as some banks seem to have been saving a little extra at the beginning of the current cash reserve arrangement," said one dealer.
The current arrangement runs from May 23 until Thursday, but a fresh cash reserve will be announced at 1400 GMT today.
"The new arrangement will probably be similar to the current one (of just over 5.01 billion guilders)," said one dealer.
Call money rates were stable at 2.75 percent bid. This is well under the current special advances rate, currently 2.90 percent, which sets the tone for money market rates.
"Call money rates will probably edge above the 3.00 percent after the new cash reserve arrangement replaces the current one," another dealer said.
The guilder was hardly changed at 112.515 per 100 marks compared to 112.505 on Monday.
Dealers said business in Dutch Treasury Certificates was negligible at current prices.
They also said the Agency of the Dutch Ministry of Finance would start selling new DTCs from Thursday.
The calendar of the Agency announces two new DTCs which start running from Thursday, one with the maturity date of September 30, 1997 and one maturing on June 30, 1998.
DTC programmes usually have a maximum issue amount of 7.5 billion guilders.
The Agency will disclose more details on Thursday.
